consumer: The frontend map painter that reads entities.items[] to render item symbols on each tile, asking 'what items would the GUI actually show on this tile?'
scope: Per-tile within the export window, gated by current visibility/LOS and map memory — only items the avatar can see now or remembers, as the GUI would draw them
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_entities(items), which iterates points_in_radius and dumps raw map::i_at(p) stacks unconditionally, with no seen/visibility or map-memory gating
divergence: An item is dropped on a tile outside the avatar's current LOS (dark or behind a wall): raw i_at reports it so the proposed surface paints it, but the GUI would show nothing there (or stale remembered contents), exposing that raw-state over-reports vs. what is displayed
